Hi Aisha — thanks again for the time today, really helpful to hear how the Clinical Notes workflow fits into your clinician experience. Quick recap and the asks we promised: 

1) What we heard (summary)
- Feature: real-time triage + summarization + structured problem list generation inside clinician chart. Triggered at note save and on-demand.
- Typical event: 3 small prompts + 1 summarization completion (~avg 1,000 tokens total per note)
- Adoption target: pilot 5k clinicians, production 20k clinicians; expected active clinicians/day ~10% of that group.

2) Asks / Info we need from you
- Range for monthly token volumes (low / mid / high) — rough is fine (tokens/month)
- Target unit economics: target $/1M tokens or target $/feature (what you want to charge per note)
- CAC/payback target for this feature (months) and any margin goals versus infrastructure cost

3) Our next steps (what we’ll deliver)
- Quick unit-econ sketch (spreadsheet attached: unit_econ_spreadsheet.xlsx) showing cost per 1M tokens at several model/quantization profiles + suggested price bands.
- Proposal for a 6–8 week pilot pricing plan and measurement cadence.

4) Proposed immediate experiment
- Pilot: 1,000 clinicians, sample week of traffic to validate average tokens/note and latency/SLOs. We can run this on a dedicated small pool to give predictable latency.

If you can reply with the rough tokens/month range and the payback window you’re targeting, we’ll fill in the spreadsheet and send a short pricing proposal for pilot + projected steady-state $/1M tokens.

Attachments: unit_econ_spreadsheet.xlsx, redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf

Thanks —
Soojin Lee

Internal notes / initial unit-econ sketch (pulling Aisha's ranges into the attached):

Baseline assumptions
- Avg tokens/note (prompt + completion + system): 1,100 tokens
- Notes/clinician/day: 2.5 -> tokens/clinician/day = 2,750 tokens
- Pilot clinicians: 1,000 -> pilot tokens/day = 2.75M tokens -> pilot tokens/month (22 working days) ~60.5M tokens
- Full roll (12k MAU): tokens/day = 33M tokens -> tokens/month (22 days) ~726M tokens

Redwood cost math (estimate per 1M tokens in common configs)
- Hosted standard model (float, no quant): $45 / 1M tokens
- Quantized (int8) friendly runtime: $18 / 1M tokens
- Aggressive optimization / batch + KV caching for prefix reuse: effective $12 / 1M tokens

Revenue targets vs cost (use Aisha's $/feature bands)
- If we price at $0.15/note and tokens/note=1,100 -> revenue/1M tokens = (1,000,000 / 1,100) * $0.15 = ~$136.36k per 1M tokens -> margin @ $18 cost = ~$118k (~86%)
- If price at $0.45/note -> revenue/1M tokens =~$409k -> margin even higher ( >95% )

CAC payback back-of-envelope (need exact CAC but using MedBridge guidance)
- Assume CAC to acquire a clinician ~ $300 (sales + onboarding)
- Monthly incremental ARPU per clinician (price $0.25/note * 2.5 notes/day * 22 days) = $137.5/month -> payback ~2.2 months at that price band.
- At lower price $0.10/note payback ~5.5 months.

Open questions / risks
- Are there hidden system tokens (server-side tools, multiple system prompts) that would increase cost? Need instrumentation during pilot.
- Embeddings / retrieval usage will add separate token/compute cost — confirm whether that’s in scope.
- Procurement will want an SLO-backed pricing band for dedicated capacity if they care about latency.

Suggested next steps (internal -> external)
- Fill the attached spreadsheet with low/mid/high token scenarios (I did a first pass, see unit_econ_spreadsheet.xlsx).
- Propose a 6-week pilot priced at an optimized rate (quantized runtime) with measurement gates at weeks 2/4/6.
- Schedule a 30-min alignment with MedBridge finance & procurement to run the margin slides and show how $/1M token bands map to their $/feature target. HubSpot deal ID: DEAL-98123

I’ll pull Marissa into pricing and Soojin can coordinate the pilot plan.

-ben
